title: Perfect-field restriction of a field groupoid morphism
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $(V,R_1,s_1,t_1,e_1,i_1,c_1)$ and $(V,R_2,s_2,t_2,e_2,i_2,c_2)$ be absolute groupoid schemes [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Let $a:R_1\to R_2$ be a morphism which, together with $\mathrm{id}_V$, commutes with all groupoid operations. There exist a field extension $k\subseteq k^{\prime}$ [def-pc-field-extension] and $V^{\prime}=\operatorname{Spec}k^{\prime}$ such that $k^{\prime}$ is perfect (in positive characteristic $p$ its Frobenius $x\mapsto x^p$ is surjective; in characteristic zero this condition is automatic) with the following properties. Put $R_j^{\prime}=V^{\prime}\times_{V,t_j}R_j\times_{s_j,V}V^{\prime}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The operations induced on test-scheme points by the operations of $R_j$ make $(V^{\prime},R_j^{\prime})$ a groupoid scheme. The induced morphism $a^{\prime}:R_1^{\prime}\to R_2^{\prime}$, equal to the identity on the two $V^{\prime}$ coordinates and to $a$ on the arrow coordinate, commutes with these operations. For $j=1,2$ the arrow-coordinate projection $q_j:R_j^{\prime}\to R_j$ is a homeomorphism on underlying topological spaces, and $q_2\circ a^{\prime}=a\circ q_1$. No finiteness hypothesis on $R_j$ or $a$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-purely-inseparable-overfield] to $k$. Choose its perfect extension $k^{\prime}/k$, which is purely inseparable: each element has a $p^n$-power in $k$ in characteristic $p>0$, and the extension is the identity in characteristic zero. Set $g:V^{\prime}=\operatorname{Spec}k^{\prime}\to V$. This choice is independent of $R_1,R_2,a$.

source.place: Tag 046W (lemma-perfection), existence; Tag 04Q9 (more-groupoids, lemma-locally-closed-image-is-closed), first proof paragraph.

proof.text: Fix $j$ and suppress the subscript. By [def-pc-fibre-product], an $H$-point of $R^{\prime}$ is a triple $(x,r,y)$ with $gx=t(r)$ and $s(r)=gy$. Define $t^{\prime}(x,r,y)=x$, $s^{\prime}(x,r,y)=y$, $e^{\prime}(x)=(x,e(gx),x)$, $i^{\prime}(x,r,y)=(y,i(r),x)$, and $c^{\prime}((x,r,y),(y,u,z))=(x,c(r,u),z)$. The identities $se=te=\mathrm{id}$, $si=t$, $ti=s$, $sc(r,u)=s(u)$ and $tc(r,u)=t(r)$ from [def-a1-groupoid-scheme] show that these tuples satisfy the fibre-product equations. Each component is a morphism (for composition use the unique map to $R\times_{s,V,t}R$ with components $r,u$), so the fibre-product universal property constructs the indicated scheme morphisms.

source.place: Tag 02VB (lemma-restrict-groupoid), construction; details of the omitted proof.

proof.text: These operations satisfy [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. On test-scheme points, composing with either displayed identity leaves $(x,r,y)$ unchanged because it leaves $r$ unchanged. Composing a triple and its inverse gives $(y,e(gy),y)$ or $(x,e(gx),x)$, respectively. For three composable triples, both associative composites retain the same outer endpoints and have middle coordinates $c(c(r,u),v)$ and $c(r,c(u,v))$, equal by the original groupoid law. The source and target laws follow directly from the formulas in step 2. Fibre-product uniqueness identifies morphisms with these equal coordinates. All formulas commute with precomposition in $H$ because their components are morphisms. This supplies the required groupoid schemes for both values of $j$.

source.place: Tag 02VB (lemma-restrict-groupoid), groupoid axioms and test-scheme interpretation; details of the omitted proof.

proof.text: The commutation of $a$ with $s,t$ gives $a^{\prime}(x,r,y)=(x,a(r),y)$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. It preserves the two endpoint projections. For identities and inverses, its middle coordinates are $a(e_1(gx))=e_2(gx)$ and $a(i_1(r))=i_2(a(r))$; for a composable pair its middle coordinate is $a(c_1(r,u))=c_2(a(r),a(u))$. Endpoints agree in each equation, so fibre-product uniqueness proves commutation with all the restricted operations. Finally both $q_2\circ a^{\prime}$ and $a\circ q_1$ send $(x,r,y)$ to $a(r)$, giving the asserted equality of morphisms.

proof.text: For either $j$, put $B_j=R_j\times_{s_j,V}V^{\prime}$, with projection $b_j:B_j\to R_j$. By [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep] applied to the $k$-scheme $(R_j,s_j)$, $b_j$ is a homeomorphism. Regard $B_j$ also as a $k$-scheme via $t_j\circ b_j$. Its base change along the same purely inseparable extension has projection $d_j:V^{\prime}\times_{V,t_j\circ b_j}B_j\to B_j$, again a homeomorphism by that lemma. By [def-pc-fibre-product], the domain of $d_j$ is canonically $R_j^{\prime}$ and $q_j=b_j\circ d_j$: both universal properties specify the same three projections and equations. Hence $q_j$ is a homeomorphism, with continuous inverse $d_j^{-1}\circ b_j^{-1}$. No finite-type, quasi-compactness or finiteness condition was used.
